Hello, this is my first post. My name is Dante, I am 26, and I am an engineer, student, musician, and aspiring physicist. This is the first post on my blog so it's probably a good place to explain what my intentions are for this page.

Over that past few years I've used my website as a place to compile and track some of the projects I've worked on, as well as a place to keep tools that I've developed to help me learn and grow. With the new year now here, I have set a few goals for myself and I'm hoping that having a place to track and organize my progress towards these goals will give me extra motivation. From time to time I may make other sorts of posts like opinion pieces, blurbs about projects I'm working on, or other things that come to mind that I'd like to speak about, but the core (for the time being) will be documentation of my progress towards my goals this year.

As I whipped this site up yesterday (the last day of 2025) in preparation for the new year, these posts are going to be very bare bones, but I intend to drastically increase the quality of them as time goes on. Right now each post has just a text section, but in the future I intend on implementing LaTeX rendering (like I have in my notes-taking website), media embedding, and even interactive code snippets. While it would be super easy to make an individual html page for each post and just plop media and text in exactly where I want it, that would be very time consuming and I generally prefer to make more generalized codebases. To that end, each of these blog posts is being generated dynamically from a single json file that contains the data for each post. This makes it much easier to organize and store the post data but it requires more complicated code to automatically generate and format the web page depending on the contents of the json file. To that end, expect the first few posts to be pretty simple as I add new features to the website. As this is primarily for tracking my growth through 2026 (and beyond if all goes well), I don't expect anybody to actually be reading this, but if you are, thank you for your time and I hope you have a good 2026.
